notes: Gross sales, orders, units and AOV: Norce ORDERED data (order date, Stockholm day, every status except 6, all Babyshop + Lekmer applications), same definition as the Daily performance tab. Gross sales = MERCHANDISE ex VAT, excluding freight, because the forecast's Gross Sales line excludes shipping; freight is ~2% on top. Gross of returns, like the plan line. Complete days only (norce-sync closes yesterday at 03:00).

Net sales = Norce merchandise − Business Central returns (credit memos incl. compensation, as in the Executive P&L). BC books a return on its POSTING date, when it is processed, not on the original order date: early-month returns are mostly October orders, and Black Week returns land in December. MTD returns are BC's actual amount per market, spread over days and brands by Norce gross (BC has no shop dimension).

GP1 = net sales − COGS at Business Central's cost-of-goods rate for the same month to date, per market (item-ledger COGS ÷ BC gross, scaled to the GL COGS the Executive P&L uses), applied to Norce merchandise. Chosen over the Funnel GM1 because it is Finance's own ledger; it is a rate, not a daily BC figure, because BC posts on invoice date and the snapshot is per month and market.

GP2 = GP1 − direct variable cost, like the forecast's GP2 line (net shipping + fulfilment + transaction fees). Measured: Norce freight income, the Shipping cost tab's modelled outbound carrier cost per order per application (last 28 days of the model), pick & pack + packaging per order from the shipping tab (contract rate; PostNord's billed rate runs ~18% lower). Carried AT FORECAST at the forecast's rate per krona of sales (no variance): warehousing, inbound/outbound/returns VAS, returns handling, return shipping, other shipping and transaction fees, 2.63 M in the November forecast = 5.0% of gross sales.
GP3 = GP2 − de-duplicated Funnel ad cost. COS% stays Funnel ad cost ÷ Funnel gross.

Last year (Nov 2025) on the same ladder: Norce merchandise × BC's Nov 2025 return and COGS rates per market, minus BC's posted Nov 2025 net shipping + fulfilment + transaction fees per order. The shipping model starts Jan 2026, so LY uses the ledger instead.

Targets: Finance's November forecast (budget_2026.json) spread per day by November 2025's daily shape, lined up by event (Black Friday, Cyber Monday, payday, weekday) with the KV Overview's own daily_targets model. We use that event-aligned shape rather than last month's, because October has no Black Friday peak; the October-shaped curve is a toggle for comparison.

The KV Overview's version of the same model pulls last year's shape 70% toward a flat month (tuned on Feb-Jul, months without Black Friday). In November that puts ~10% of the month into 1-3 Nov instead of last year's 5% and flattens the Black Friday peak, so it reads far behind early in the month. This tab uses the full shape; the 'KV Overview model' toggle shows the other one. Monthly totals are identical.

Scope: the forecast covers Babyshop + Lekmer combined (verified against BC, Finance's ledger: Jun-Sep 2026 posted gross 103.6 M vs Norce Babyshop + Lekmer 103.1 M vs Babyshop alone 96.9 M). Actuals cover the same scope.

Market and brand targets: the forecast is global only, so each market's and brand's target is the global target × its share of the same metric in Nov 2025 (event-aligned, on this tab's own ladder; ad cost on the Funnel mix). Norce market = the ordering application (SE/NO/FI/DK incl. Lekmer; EU, UK, NA, Asia, ROW apps = ROW). Market GP3 = market GP2 − market ad cost. The mix has moved a lot since then (NO and DK roughly doubled in Oct 2026 YoY; international revenue moved from 'ROW EUR' to named countries), so per-market targets are a rough guide: NO/DK read ahead, ROW reads behind.

1 Nov: All Saints' Day fell on 1 Nov 2025 but on 31 Oct 2026, so 1 Nov 2026 has no last-year twin and the model gives it an average-day target × the Sunday factor (~1.9 M). It reads behind on that day for that reason.

Spend headroom: the binding target is the forecast's GP3 (8.48 M), not its 10.5% COS, which is derived from assumed GM1 38.4% / GM2 26.5%. Allowed spend = GP2 − GP3 target (MTD on the daily curve; month on landing GP2 at the current run-rate). Headroom = allowed − actual (MTD) and allowed − expected spend at run-rate (rest of month), spread by the marketing index. Extra spend only keeps GP3 if it adds at least as much incremental GP2 as it costs. GP2 and margins are on this tab's own ladder (Norce − BC − shipping model). Per market it rides the Nov 2025 mix split: the forecast itself has no market split.
GM1 caveat: Business Central books returns when they are processed, so GM1/GM2 (and the headroom built on them) run high during a sales peak until the peak's returns land, largely in December.

Marketing cost = ALL marketing cost in the Funnel export, every channel with cost (Google, Meta, affiliate, Naver, price comparison, ...), de-duplicated with bq_source's COST_GRAIN machinery. The forecast's marketing line (5.54 M) is entirely 'Marketing ad spend' (other marketing and marketing consultants are 0) and equals Funnel's all-channel cost for Nov 2025 (5.537 M) to 0.01%, so the scope matches. Business Central's GL booked 4.71 M marketing for Nov 2025; that gap to Funnel is not reconciled here. Funnel is the basis, as instructed.
Last year = same weekday 364 days earlier, so Black Friday 27 Nov lines up with 28 Nov 2025 and Cyber Monday 30 Nov with 1 Dec 2025.
Landing = MTD actual + remaining daily target × the last 7 complete days' actual/target ratio.

New vs returning: Norce orders on order date; new = the customer's first-ever order in that shop. Norce history starts 11 Jun 2025, so last year's 'new' is overstated (anyone who last bought before June 2025 counts as new). Revenue there is merchandise ex shipping, so new + returning = Norce gross sales MTD.
